newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht nervous after Amnuay departure.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht nervous after Amnuay departure.

text.p: The Thai baht remained under pressure on Friday amid concern about the government's economic policies following the abrupt resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan.
Dealers said the dollar was well bid against the baht in both domestic and offshore spot markets, while forwards moved to the left.
"The market still feels the shock effect of Amnuay's departure. People turn cautious by holding on to the safer dollars," a local bank dealer in Bangkok said.

Amnuay resigned on Thursday over differences in economic policies with political rivals in Thailand's six-party coalition government. Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also tendered his resignation, effective June 21.

The baht eased to 25.900/26.010 to the dollar at 0420 GMT in the domestic market from 25.835/25.845 late on Wednesday. The central bank fixed the midrate at 25.79 per dollar against 25.77 on Thursday.
In the offshore market, the baht fell to 25.200/25.700 from 24.250/24.300 late on Thursday.
Dealers in Singapore said some offshore players were taking short baht positions on concern about the economic fallout from Amnuay's departure.
"The market is speculating that over the weekend, Thailand will actually devalue the currency. So the dollar remain very well bid," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said the dollar would be well supported around 25.100 baht and should head back towards 26.000 soon.

The dealer said softer forward rates were encouraging players to go long dollars as the carry cost was not as expensive as it has been since the Bank of Thailand (BOT) moved to limit the supply of baht in overseas markets in mid-May.
The BOT has repeatedly ruled out a baht devaluation. It said on Thursday there was no need to fear one after Amnuay's departure.
Analysts say a baht devaluation could lead to further capital account outflows and increase the debt burden of ailing firms in the finance sector.

"The fundamentals haven't changed and corporates remain weak from the overseas liabilities burden so a devaluation now would cure nothing at all," said Chiang Yao Chye, economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in Singapore.
The Singapore dollar slipped in reaction to an unexpected decline in the country's exports for May.

The Trade Development Board said Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell a nominal 1.0 pct percent year-on-year in May compared to the same month in the previous year. Non-oil domestic exports rose 5.9 percent in April.
A Reuter poll of 10 Singapore-based economists had predicted a nominal year-on-year rise of 3.5 percent in May.
But dealers said the U.S. dollar would remain toppish around 1.4290 against the Singapore dollar as uncertainty in regional currency markets generated demand for the relatively stable Singapore unit.

"I think there would be inflows to the Sing for its safe haven status, especially with the baht and rupiah weakening," a dealer said. The Singapore dollar was at 1.4261/71 to the U.S. unit at 0420 GMT.
The Malaysian ringgit showed a firmer tone following reports of comments by acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim that the spillover effects from the baht would be temporary.
Anwar, also finance minister, was quoted by Malaysian newspapers as saying the context of the ringgit and the baht, and the economic fundamentals in Malaysia and Thailand were different.
"The market sold dollars against ringgit on Anwar's comments from 2.5160 down to the 2.5115 level. But we've seen some buying at 2.5110 and below," a Singapore dealer said.
Dealers said the ringgit might test the 2.5100 level through the day and possibly slip down towards 2.5080.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5131/41 to the dollar at 0415 GMT.
The Indonesian rupiah succumbed to offshore selling interest after strengthening briefly to the 2,430.0 level on the back of tighter money market liquidity.

"The tone remains biddish on the dollar but we see some selling orders at the 2,432.0 level. If it does break, we are heading towards the next resistance level at 2,435," one dealer said. Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,431.5/32.5 at 0420 GMT.
Dealers said the market remained cautious due to continued political and economic uncertainties in Thailand.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703090)
